quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, lane markings, and metal covers are hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement provides the best grip.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. In hot weather, leather jackets help protect you from dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for items made of:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the highest level of protection.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare.
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead of your motorcycle to spot hazards early. This helps you react safely before you reach them.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same lane position all the time.
Move around the lane to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No one lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms.

questions.question: When riding at night, do all of the following except:

options.text: Use headlights from cars ahead to see farther down the road.
Use your high beam headlight when appropriate.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam when not following or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: To help others see you as a motorcycle rider, you should:
questions.explanation: To be seen, wear bright colors, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, slow down and keep your motorcycle upright. Go over the surface as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the proper body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This position lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: What can help other drivers see your motorcycle at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to draw attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight to increase visibility at intersections. Ride in a position that gives other drivers a clear view of your motorcycle. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take evasive action.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
No protective clothing for the passenger.
A sticker on the brake light warning of a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who has a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It tells you about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: Which riders are most likely to crash?

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: Why is a cushion of space around your motorcycle important?

options.text: To give you time to react to hazards.
To hide you from other drivers.
To prevent you from avoiding hazards.
To allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A cushion of space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need the space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If you wear laced boots, tuck the laces away securely before riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes. Do it once a month.
A few minutes. Do it before every ride.
Over an hour. A mechanic must do it.
Over an hour. Only do it if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes. Do it before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider become more visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. Paint damage is not a safety concern for riding.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
Other drivers may want the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle can also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look only at the road directly ahead.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns toward where you want to go. Turn only your head and eyes, not your shoulders. Keep your arms slightly bent and your knees against the tank for balance. Watch for hazards ahead, behind, and to the sides.
